To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
allele-specific silencings of mutant ataxian-7, targeting an SNP, has been successfully demonstrated in patient-derived fibroblast cells.

allele-specific silenc-ing of mutant Atax-7 in primary SCA7 patient fibroblasts is feasible and that it is associated with restoration of the expression of two disease-related transcripts, UCHL-1 and DNAJA-1.

1) allele-specific silencing was achieved using two siRNA sequences targeting a common SNP within the SCA7 gene in SCA7 patients; 2) two disease-relevant genes were identified as altered in SCA7 primary patient fibroblasts, and 3) siRNA-mediated silencing of mutant SCA7 restored the levels of these disease-relevant genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapies for the treatment of neurodegenerative disorders, including Huntington’s Disease (HD) and Spinocerebellar Ataxia 7 (SCA 7).
the development of RNAi-based therapies for the treatment of polyQ disorders, including SCA7.
the development of allele-specific RNAi as a therapeutic strategy for the polyQ diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work has shown the feasibility of using RNAi to reduce mutant Ataxin 7 in SCA patient fibroblasts.

this study provides a novel approach to study the molecular pathogenesis of SCA7 and other polyQ disorders, and provides the basis for the development of allele-specific RNAi therapeutics for SCA7 and related disorders.
the RNAi-based therapeutic strategy is a promising and feasible approach to treat polyQ diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

allele-specific silencer RNAs are a promising approach to reduce mutant ataxin levels in SCA7 patients, and that the patient-derived fibroblast cell line is a useful model for studying disease mechanisms and for testing therapeutic effectors.
we have demonstrated allele-specific silencing in SCA7 cells and we have identified two genes that are dysregulated in these cells.
allele-specific RNAi is an effective approach to target the disease causing mutation in a patient-specific manner, and that this approach may be used for the treatment of polyQ diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNAi-based therapeutics can be used as a treatment strategy in the polyQ disorders.

allele-specific silences can be used to reduce levels of toxic mutant proteins in a disease-relevant cellular context, and that this approach can be used to measure the efficacy of RNAi in primary patient cell models.
allele-specific RNAi is a viable approach for treating SCA7 and potentially other polyQ disorders.
